round2FixVerification.FIND-R2-001_startup_seed_forged_FIRING: FIXED AND VERIFIED. gig-cli.sh:36 now touches ~/gig/.last-start only. The STARTUP prompt instructs the model to touch ~/gig/.last-pass in its FINALLY clause only after a real completed pass, with the explicit guard 'never touch it on mere startup/restart'. The --restart path (gig-cli.sh:27) kills the session and then falls through to line 34-36, touching .last-start but not .last-pass. The auditor's FIRING verdict is now derived from a file that startup/restart CANNOT forge.
round2FixVerification.FIND-R2-002_restart_storm: FIXED AND VERIFIED. gig-healthcheck.sh:15-32: restart() counts RESTART_LOG timestamps within the last 3600s; if count >= 5, logs backoff and returns without restarting. The log entry (line 29, echo "$now") is written only when count < 5 and a restart proceeds. The window is sliding (based on age from current time), not fixed, so entries age out naturally — the backoff is not permanent: once the earliest entry exceeds 3600s old, count drops below 5 and restarts resume. The maximum restart rate is 5 per 3600-second window.
round2FixVerification.FIND-R2-003_no_heartbeat_branch_near_unr: FIXED (INTERACTION FIX) AND VERIFIED. gig-healthcheck.sh:36-45: when .last-pass is absent AND tmux is alive, the branch now reads START_AGE from .last-start mtime. If START_AGE < 90 (STALE_MIN), it logs 'ALIVE (first pass pending)' and does NOT restart. Only if START_AGE >= 90 does it restart. Since gig-cli.sh:36 touches .last-start on every (re)start, START_AGE resets to ~0 after each restart, giving a genuine 90-minute grace window before the next no-heartbeat restart — the restart loop described in the INTERACTION FIX is eliminated. Verified: fresh-boot path (small START_AGE) does not restart; long-booted-no-pass path (START_AGE >= 90) does restart.
round2FixVerification.FIND-R2-004_delta_mislabel: FIXED AND VERIFIED. auditor.sh:39-55: (a) the output key is now 'actions_delta_since_last_audit' (was 'applied_delta_since_last_audit'); (b) prev_actions is obtained from prev_last.get('actions_total') which returns None if the previous row has no such key; (c) when prev_actions is None (first audit or post-migration first row), actions_delta is set to 0 and progressing is set to False — no spurious full-count delta on first run. The old bug (prev_actions or 0 = 0 on first run, yielding actions_delta = full count) is gone.
round2FixVerification.FIND-R2-005_jpy_crash: FIXED AND VERIFIED. jnum(v) helper present in all three scripts: auditor.sh:21-23, monitor.sh:19-21, run.sh:24-27. The helper does str(v).replace(',','').replace('¥','').replace('円','').strip() or 0, wrapped in try/except returning 0.0 on any exception. Non-numeric jpy values (e.g. '5,000', '¥5,000円', None) are coerced to 0.0 and cannot crash the script. All three scripts use jnum() in both the filter and the sum.

newDefectSearch.permanent_wedge_from_restart_log: NOT A WEDGE. RESTART_LOG entries age out of the 3600s sliding window naturally. After count reaches 5 and backoff fires, the entry window begins to drain: within at most 3600s from the oldest of the 5 entries, count drops to 4 and restarts resume. Confirmed by tracing: entries are only appended (line 29) when count < 5, so the 5 entries in the window span at most 3600s, and after 3600+1s from the first, count drops. The log file grows indefinitely (~60 bytes/hour max) but this is not a correctness concern.
newDefectSearch.last_start_resets_START_AGE_on_every_res: ANALYZED. YES, .last-start is refreshed every restart (gig-cli.sh:36). In the NO-HEARTBEAT case this resets START_AGE to ~0, giving a new 90-minute grace window. This does NOT create a permanent wedge: the restart rate in the no-heartbeat case is at most once per 90 minutes (the grace window IS the rate limiter), which is 0.67/hour — far below the backoff threshold of 5/hour. In the STALE case (.last-pass exists and old), .last-start is also refreshed but the STALE branch does not use START_AGE, so restarts can fire every 5 minutes (healthcheck cadence) until the backoff (5/hour) kicks in. This is the designed aggressive behavior for a stale core.
